newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Spot Prods--Gulf gasoline bullish at deadline.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Spot Prods--Gulf gasoline bullish at deadline.

text.p: Gulf Coast regular unleaded gasoline was again the top story in U.S. spot refined oil products markets, with differentials firming up ahead of a pipeline scheduling deadline, traders said.
New York Harbor and midcontinent markets were meanwhile terribly quiet in early trade.

Underlying NYMEX futures prices meanwhile retreated following Wednesday's OPEC-inspired gains amid scepticism that the 11-country oil producing group will actually be able to adhere to its output ceiling as it pledged to do during its meeting in Vienna.
U.S. GULF COAST

Regular unleaded conventional gasoline was again the top story in Houston where refiners, as is often the case, were lining up to buy ahead of a Colonial Pipeline scheduling deadline at the end today's trading.

The nature of the buying interest was however a bit puzzling, since there are now no major plant outages in the region's dense refining infrastructure, and most prevailing views hold that near-record gasoline output in recent weeks has left the country rather well supplied.
"I'm at a loss as to explaining why there's buying," said one gasoline trader.
Differentials on prompt M1 firmed by more than a cent in morning trade to 1.85 cents under August NYMEX unleaded, though no deals at those freshly firmer levels could be immediately confirmed.

Some traders guessed that the heavy refiner interest in gasoline could be that they are trying to prepare for the heavier gasoline demand that is likely to accompany the upcoming three-day U.S. Inpendence Day holiday that begins in just over a week.

Additionally, traders are beginning to think that refiners need to be buying on the spot market because demand at the pump has actually turned out to be as robust as the industry data has suggested in its surveys.

Those data, which track the relatively abstract notion of 'implied demand' by measuring movement of inventories out of primary storage like refinery tank farms, are often criticized for their inaccuracies.
NEW YORK HARBOR
The summer doldrums continued Thursday morning, with differentials for most products talked at stable levels from Wednesday amid a distinct lack of activity.
"There's nothing happening -- nothing, nothing, nothing," one East Coast player said, adding he had plenty of time to catch up on other chores since he didn't have to deal with a ringing telephone.

NYH "M2" conventional unleaded gasoline was offered at 3.0 cents below June futures, a tad weaker than Wednesday diffs, while "A2" reformulated held steady at 0.50 cent under the screen, traders said.
NYH heating oil and low sulfur diesel diffs were also stable, at 0.20 cent below the print and a half cent over the screen, respectively, traders said.
U.S. MIDCONTINENT:

Markets were quiet in the Midcontinent amid a lack of interest and news. Prompt June unleaded gasoline differentials in Group Three were pegged unchanged at 4.00/4.50 cents over July. Prompt July in Chicogo was also unchanged, with deals done at 0.60 cents over the print.
Low sulfur diesel in Chicago weakened a quarter cent amid a drop in agricultural demand. Group Three barrels, however, remained stable with offers at 2.25 cents over July heating oil.
-- New York Oil Desk 1 212 859 1633
